title: NRC OKs Westinghouse AP1000 design certification revision, renewal
summary: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission has approved Westinghouse’s request to renew and update the standard design certification (DC) for its AP1000 reactor. Wednesday’s renewal allows Westinghouse to incorporate the lessons learned from the construction of Vogtle-3 and -4 in Georgia into the design of the AP1000, establishing Vogtle-4 as the standard AP1000 reference plant for U.S. deployment. The DC renewal should further Westinghouse’s efforts to make repeated deployments of its AP1000—a reactor that is a key player in domestic efforts to quadruple nuclear capacity over the next few decades—more rapid and efficient.

title: Sweden’s Studsvik Signs ‘Landmark’ Spent Nuclear Fuel Agreement With Norway
summary: Sweden-based nuclear services company Studsvik has signed what it called a “landmark” agreement to manage Norway’s legacy spent nuclear fuel. The agreement with Norwegian Nuclear Decommissioning (NND), the Norwegian state agency responsible for decommissioning the country’s nuclear facilities, runs until 2055 and has an estimated contractual minimum value of about SEK 875m (€78m, $88m) and a potential total value for Studsvik of SEK 3-4bn. It covers transport, treatment of waste to meet long-term storage requirements and the interim storage of spent fuel from Norway’s former research reactors at Halden and Kjeller.

title: Oklo announces plans for Groves-2
summary: This week, Oklo revealed the details of the next chapter of its Groves project. Those plans will build on the company’s previous progress through the Department of Energy’s Reactor Pilot Program, will be enabled by the DOE’s follow-on Nuclear Energy Launch Pad Program, and will focus initially on medical isotope production.

title: Molten salt–fueled reactor experiment approved for DOE cost-shared funding
summary: Yesterday, Southern Company and Core Power announced that the Department of Energy approved cost-shared funding through the Advanced Reactor Demonstration Program (ARDP) for an accelerated final stage of the Molten Chloride Reactor Experiment (MCRE), which the companies are conducting in collaboration with Idaho National Laboratory. According to the announcement, MCRE could achieve criticality as early as 2027, which could be a world-first: To date, no fast-spectrum molten chloride salt reactor has reached criticality.

title: Maritime Nuclear Startup Bluecore Buys First Uranium For Nuclear Plants On Barges
summary: Bluecore Energy, the Long Beach, US-based floating nuclear power startup, has bought its first supply of uranium hexafluoride (UF6), a low-enriched 4.95% blend of U-235 suitable for a commercial nuclear power installation. The material is being held at a US nuclear fuel facility outside the state of California while Bluecore advances its plans for future fuel fabrication, testing and validation. UF6 is the required form of uranium during the enrichment stage of the nuclear fuel cycle. During the fuel fabrication stage, the UF6 is converted into uranium dioxide, or UO2, which can then be fabricated into fuel pellets and assembled into nuclear fuel. The purchase follows Bluecore’s recent $50m (€44m) seed financing.
